assumptions: Uniform printed plastic; mass bias comes only from the fat ventral volume and the planar cut.
A tabletop flick on a hard surface is enough to lift the face onto the belly.
Digital geometry cannot prove the audible knock; the rim and face are designed for that event.

build_plan.exit_criteria: The knockseed STL exists with the ventral knock face at Z=0, a rounded belly, and a pumpkin-seed silhouette, as one printable solid.

components.duty: Receives a fingertip flick, spins on the rounded belly, and returns to the ventral knock face with a knock.
components.form: Solid seed body 36.1 mm long, 18.4 mm wide, and 12.7 mm tall, with a rounded micropyle bead at +X, a planar ventral knock face at Z=0, and a rounded equatorial belly.
components.interfaces: None. The ventral oval is the table contact; the equatorial bulge is the spin contact.
components.name: knockseed
components.placement: Prints as one piece standing on the ventral knock face at Z=0 mm; no other parts.

concept.interaction: Pinch the knockseed, set it on a table, and flick the equator. It turns on the rounded belly, then gravity pulls the heavy ventral side down until the oval knock face meets the table with a soft knock. The same face is the only rest pose. Pick it up and flick again; there is no reset part.

novel_mechanisms.definition: A one-piece solid whose center of mass sits toward a single rest face so gravity returns the body to that face after a spin or tilt.
A convex equatorial bulge that becomes the rolling contact under a fingertip flick, letting the seed turn on its belly before gravity recaptures it.
A bounded oval rest face, distinct from the belly curve, whose outer rim meets the table first and produces a knock at the end of the settle.

concept.print_stance: Ventral knock face on the bed at Z=0 mm. The rounded belly rises from that face so the print is support-free.
risks: If the rest face is too large the seed will not stay on the belly long enough to spin.
If the rest face is too small it becomes a weeble point and the knock face disappears.
A knife-edge rim would fail thickness; the rest-face perimeter stays at least 1.6 mm of solid.
concept.signature_decision: Two contacts on one body: a rounded belly for the spin and a distinct oval face that always knocks down. A spherical weeble would hide the face; a coin-spinner would not prefer one face.
concept.summary: A fingertip-sized one-piece seed that spins on a rounded belly after a flick and always knocks to rest on the same ventral face.
concept.title: Knockseed

decisions: Selected Pico Press because the magic is the compact spin-and-settle cycle, not a machine, a science lesson, or an acoustic instrument.
Rejected a fully spherical weeble because it would rest on the same curve it spins on, hiding the promised face and knock.
Rejected a two-part weighted insert because the Wish asks for one piece.
research.hardest_to_fake_magic: A fingertip flick that turns the seed on its rounded belly, then a gravity-biased settle onto one face that ends in a soft knock.
notes: Self-righting tumblers return to one pose when the center of mass sits toward that rest face, so any other orientation raises the mass.
A planar cut on an otherwise convex belly creates two contacts: rolling on the curve during spin, knocking on the face at rest.
One-piece FDM cannot add a metal weight. Mass bias is produced by putting more solid volume toward the rest face and using that face as the print bed.
